best_section.where: kerb beside the bowls green/tennis courts, roughly two-thirds of the way down Keith St from the Sir Fred Schonell Dr corner, opposite the sports centre

drivers.seclusion: This stretch backs onto bowls greens and tennis courts behind a hedge, not house frontages; across the road is a sports/community centre, not homes. Houses further up near the Sir Fred Schonell Dr corner sit close to the kerb (within ~20m) and are poorer.
drivers.access_and_room: Sealed kerbside lane, screened by a continuous hedge row, no driveways or crossings crossing it in this stretch; plenty of straight room for a long van.
drivers.traffic: OSM tags this residential but it carries 3 lanes and a 50 km/h limit, more like a loop service road for the sports precinct than a quiet street; could see through-traffic at night.
drivers.convention: Multiple cars already parked nose-to-tail along this exact stretch in both the Esri and QLD imagery, so a van won't stand out.

flags: Wider/faster road than typical residential (3 lanes, 50 km/h signed) despite existing on-street parking
Grade of roughly 2-3% through this section, within the gentle range
Houses near the northern end of the kerb (first ~40m) sit close behind trees — avoid that part
sun_shade: Overhung by the roadside hedge/tree line on the west (parking) side most of the day; some afternoon sun may reach through gaps from the west.
cannot_judge: Kerb height/crossfall for levelling the van
Whether on-site signage adds restrictions beyond the sign screen
Actual night-time traffic volume on this loop road
reasons: Backs onto sports fields, not houses
Cars already parked along this stretch
Road is wider/faster than a typical quiet street
summary: Secluded kerb beside bowls/tennis courts with cars already parked, let down by a surprisingly wide, 50 km/h road.
